text:
jen: Customer reports duplicate POSTs and billing spikes after SDK retries. they see 2 identical requests reach our API sometimes when network blips happen.

ben: which SDK and node version? any proxy in front?

jen: ts-sdk@1.13.0, node 20.4, hosted customer on Vercel (serverless). No custom proxy reported. Error flow: transient socket reset -> SDK retries -> server sees duplicate payloads.

carmen: can you paste the client call + retry config and whether the body is a stream/readable?

jen: here's anonymized snippet:```ts
const res = await client.responses.create({
  model: 'redwood/gpt-large',
  input: streamBody, // Readable from file upload
  retry: { maxRetries: 2, backoff: 200 }
});
```

ben: aha, reusing a Readable stream + retry can cause duplication if the implementation re-sends the same stream instance. Also AbortSignal semantics differ between undici and global fetch in node20.

danny: additionally, undici's fetch will throw if signal is already aborted; some retry wrappers re-use the same AbortController which causes weird timing races.

jen: customer logs: shows first request got ECONNRESET at 2075550005, client retried at 2075550010 and server received second POST. No idempotency-key header present.

carmen: immediate mitigation: advise them to 1) avoid streaming body reuse (buffer or recreate stream per attempt) 2) add an idempotency header for POSTs 3) ensure a fresh AbortController per try.

jen: any SDK changes needed? they want an SDK-backed fallback so they don't have to modify app code.

ben: short-term SDK guidance: document that body must be re-creatable for retries and show pattern to buffer or use file path -> create stream inside retry logic. Long-term we should detect non-replayable bodies and skip automatic retries for them.

carmen: repro notes I ran locally: node 20.4, undici 5.11.0, ts-sdk@1.13.0. Repro steps: create Readable from fs.createReadStream, trigger artificial socket reset (iptables REJECT) -> SDK retries -> second POST observed.

ben: root cause (summary): combination of 1) reusing a non-idempotent request body (stream) across retries and 2) mismatch between how our retry wrapper handles AbortController and undici/global fetch signal behavior. When the first attempt's signal is aborted by socket error, we were reusing the same controller for subsequent tries which in some edge cases left the retry path without a fresh signal, causing immediate resend or odd timing.

jen: proposed fixes: - patch ts-sdk to create a fresh AbortController per retry attempt - detect stream bodies and opt-out of automatic retries or buffer when configured - add idempotency-key recommendation in docs & examples

carmen: I opened internal issue INF-2489 to track. adding a small PR to ts-sdk that: 1) clones retry logic to instantiate new AbortController per iteration, 2) emits a warning when body is a ReadableStream and retries>0.

ben: also bump undici to 5.12.0 in our test matrix — some signal handling fixes landed there.

deploy-bot: deploy queued for branch fix/inf-2489 to staging at 2075550600 by carmen.

jen: customer notified with mitigation steps and asked to try buffered upload or add idempotency-key. will follow up.

carmen: quick patch landed in PR #4123 that avoids retrying when content-type indicates multipart/form-data or when body is instance of stream.Readable. We added a CLI flag in the SDK `retries.replayableBodiesOnly` default true.

ben: tests added to cover node20 global fetch + undici combos.

jen: customer confirmed they switched to buffering and duplicates stopped. they also accepted rollout to include SDK patch.

danny: follow-up item: create a short doc snippet showing how to implement idempotency-key header pattern and example for streams.

jen: thanks all, marking resolved for this thread. :white_check_mark:
